items.title: Why airplane windows have a tiny hole
items.summary: Why airplane windows have a tiny hole. Cruise altitude air is about 3.4 psi and the cabin is about 11, so each window is pushed outward with roughly 8 psi. The hole in the middle pane lets cabin air reach the outer pane, which carries the load. Sources: ScienceAlert (GKN Aerospace, American Vacuum Society), FAA 14 CFR 25.841. items.title: Why cracking your knuckles doesn't cause arthritis
items.summary: Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis? Dr. Donald Unger cracked only his left hand's knuckles for more than 60 years and kept the right as a control. Neither hand developed arthritis, and he won the 2009 Ig Nobel Prize in Medicine. In 2015, researchers filmed a knuckle crack in a real-time MRI and saw the crack come as a cavity formed in the joint. Sources: Ig Nobel Prize 2009 (Improbable Research); Kawchuk GN et al., "Real-Time Visualization of Joint Cavitation", PLOS ONE 10(4), 2015. Idea: AsapSCIENCE. Which knuckle do you crack first? #Shorts #health #science

items.summary: Bro sells his software for $3K a month and says it’s “very affordable.” Meet Oliver. He scaled Tabs Chocolate to $11M a year and sold it for millions. Now he runs Bustem, a mix of AI agents and real people that finds and takes down copycats, counterfeits, and unauthorized resellers for e-commerce brands. “We do this for 1,500 bucks to $5,000 a month on average, about 3K a month. So very affordable.”
